name: sg-haze
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's haze: a drifting colour field quantised into flat bands and stippled at the edges, so the section reads as a low-bit gradient catching light rather than a smooth blend.

colors.description: A four-stop ramp, darkest first: the shader quantises one field into bands and reads the ramp with it, so the order matters more here than in the pole-based backgrounds. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

driftSpeed.description: How fast the haze drifts; 0 holds the bands still. Upstream default, range 0 to 0.6.

steps.description: How many colour bands the field is quantised into. Low is a bold poster, high approaches a smooth ramp. Upstream default, range 2 to 24.

softness.description: Scale of the underlying field; low gives big banks, high gives more of them. Upstream default, range 0.3 to 2.

dither.description: Ordered stipple that breaks the band edges up instead of leaving hard contours. 0 gives clean posterised steps. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.5.

deviations.what: The four u_palette ramp stops are ours, not upstream's `dusk` preset.
deviations.why: haze/meta.json names a palette as a string only; the table it resolves against lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Ours is a muted dusk ordered dark to light, because the shader reads the four as a ramp rather than as independent poles.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs grain 0.06, vignette 0.22 and saturation 1.04 over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain is also in @shader-gallery/runtime. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster. The section's own CSS grain layer covers the banding the poster's grain was there for.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
